newsitem.title: USA: Bank profits grew in third quarter, but credit woes persist.
newsitem.headline: Bank profits grew in third quarter, but credit woes persist.

text.p: Major U.S. banks, led by Chase Manhattan Corp. and Citicorp., Tuesday reported strong gains for the latest quarter, but continuing concern about consumer credit.

Chase, which overtook Citicorp this year as the nation's largest bank company after its merger with Chemical Banking Corp., said its earnings in the third quarter rose to $858 million, up 12 percent from $764 million in the same period of 1995.
Citicorp said it earned $935 million in the period, up 11 percent from $877 million a year ealier.

The results at Chase included after-tax merger-related expenses of $32 million, but merger savings in the quarter were $180 million. The company said it expects to achieve merger savings of $510 million in 1996.
Chase and Chemical merged on March 31. The year-ago comparisons were made as though the merger had been in effect for all periods.

"We continued to demonstrate revenue growth across both our global wholesale and nationwide consumer businesses," said Walter V. Shipley, chairman and chief executive officer. "We also stuck to the basics, effectively managing our operating and credit costs."
The corporation's return on average common stockholders' equity was 17.9 percent, which compared with 16.2 percent in the 1995 third quarter.
Credit card net charge-offs were $296 million, or 4.95 percent of average managed receivables. That compared with $279 million, or 4.78 percent, in the second quarter, Chase said.
Chase said its earnings were equal to $1.80 a share, compared with $1.58 a share a year earlier.
Total assets as of Sept. 30 were $323 billion, compared with $308 billion a year earlier.
For the first nine months, Chase earned $1.6 billion, or $3.28 a share, on revenue of $11.9 billion. A year yearlier, Chase earned $2.1 billion, or $4.47 a share, on revenue of $11.1 billion.
Citicorp said income from its consumer operations fell to $466 million from $515 million, partly as a result of higher costs in its credit card business.
It said charge-offs due to non-payment on credit cards were at a rate of 5.11 percent of outstanding domestic credit card debt, up from 4.99 percent in the second quarter.
U.S. bankcard loans delinquent 90 days or more were 1.86 percent of the portfolio, versus 1.73 percent at the end of the second quarter and 1.54 percent a year ago, the company said.
Its worldwide card business earned $243 million in the quarter, down from $290 million a year ago.
Citicorp said net income from its corporate banking business worldwide was $520 million versus $389 million a year ago.
The results were equal to $1.85 a share, up from $1.79 a share a year earlier.

In the first nine months, Citicorp earned $2.8 billion, or $5.53 a share, on revenue of $15.8 billion. That compared with earnings of $2.6 billion, or $5.29 a share, on revenue of $14.6 billion in the year-ago period.
Citicorp had total assets of $272 billion at the end of the third quarter, up from $257 billion on Dec. 31, 1995.
Citicorp's stock gained $1.375 to $94.75 on the New York Stock Exchange. Chase was unchanged at $82.50, also on the NYSE.
